_meta.scope: Sick Young Infant, age up to 2 months
_meta.source: IMNCI Chart Booklet for Medical Officers (2023), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Govt. of India
_meta.note: Rules paraphrased and structured from the official chart booklet. Each rule includes a reference to the chart section it maps to, for auditability.
_meta.usage: The Risk Combination Agent should check rules in order (bacterial_infection first, then jaundice, then diarrhoea, then feeding), since a single visit may trigger multiple classifications. Any 'refer_now' result takes priority over all others.

signs_any_of_age_gated.note: Fast breathing counts toward SEVERE classification only under 7 days old. For 7-59 days, it belongs to the local infection rule instead.

rules.action_summary: Refer urgently to hospital. Give pre-referral care (anticonvulsant if convulsing, first antibiotic dose if available, keep warm, prevent low blood sugar).

signs_any_of.note: applies only to infants 7-59 days old; under 7 days, fast breathing belongs to the severe classification instead

rules.action_summary: Give oral antibiotic course, teach home treatment for local infection, advise when to return immediately, follow up after 2 days.
rules.escalate_if: infant also has low_weight_for_age or another severe classification present

rules.condition: none of the above bacterial infection signs present
rules.action_summary: Advise home care for the young infant.

signs_any_of.condition: jaundice present (any onset/extent) AND infant age >= 14 days

rules.action_summary: Refer urgently to hospital. Treat to prevent low blood sugar, keep warm on the way.
rules.note: Per IMNCI: any jaundice persisting to 14 days of age or beyond is classified severe regardless of extent, since physiological jaundice should have resolved by then.

rules.action_summary: Advise home care. Tell caregiver to return immediately if palms/soles turn yellow OR if the infant reaches 14 days of age with jaundice still present. Follow up after 2 days.
rules.reassurance_note: This pattern is common and usually resolves without treatment, but must still be monitored.
rules.note: Superseded by jaundice_severe if infant reaches age >= 14 days while jaundice is still present — do not independently advise referral only 'if older than 2 weeks', since that threshold is now the severe classification's trigger, not a separate soft recommendation.

rules.action_summary: Refer urgently, with ORS sips on the way if infant can drink, or Plan C rehydration if no other severe classification present.
Give Plan B fluids, escalate to urgent referral only if another severe classification also present.

rules.condition: not enough signs to classify as some or severe dehydration
rules.action_summary: Give Plan A home fluids and continue feeding, advise when to return immediately, follow up after 2 days if no improvement.

rules.chart_section: Check for Feeding Problem or Low Weight
rules.action_summary: Refer urgently to hospital. Prevent low blood sugar and keep warm via skin-to-skin contact while arranging referral.

rules.chart_section: Check for Feeding Problem or Low Weight
rules.action_summary: Counsel on correct positioning/attachment, feeding frequency, home warmth for low weight. Advise when to return immediately. Follow up after 2 days (feeding) or 14 days (low weight).

rules.chart_section: Check for Feeding Problem or Low Weight
rules.condition: weight_status is normal_weight and no other feeding signs present
rules.action_summary: Praise caregiver for feeding well, advise home care, advise when to return immediately.

confidence_weighting.note: Applied by the Risk Combination Agent on top of the above rules.
confidence_weighting.asha_reported: Use classifications as-is; ASHA input is treated as structured, trained-observer data.
confidence_weighting.parent_reported: Apply a wider safety margin: any ambiguous or unconfirmed sign that could plausibly belong to a refer_now combination should bias the outcome toward monitor_recheck or refer_now rather than reassure, until disambiguated.

universal_return_now_signs.chart_section: Advise the Mother when to return to physician
universal_return_now_signs.description: Regardless of initial classification, caregiver should be told to return immediately if any of these develop.
